Where it began

Marnus Labuschagne was born in Klerksdorp, in South Africa, on 22 June 1994. When he was 10 his family moved to Australia for his father's work, and he grew up in Brisbane speaking Afrikaans at home, picking up English after the move. He went to Brisbane State High School, played for Queensland at every junior level, and captained the state side at the 2012–13 national championships.

He sharpened his game in English club cricket too. In 2014 he scored 1,049 runs for Sandwich Town, a new record for a season in the Kent Premier League.

The player

His Test debut, against Pakistan in the United Arab Emirates in October 2018, began with a duck, though he took two wickets. The turning point came at Lord's in August 2019, when he came on for Steve Smith and became the first concussion substitute in Test history. He made 59 and kept his place.

That summer at home he made his first Test hundred, 185 at the Gabba, then 215 at Sydney in January 2020. He finished 2019 as the leading Test run-scorer in the world and was a Wisden Cricketer of the Year. In all he played 67 Tests from 2018 to 2026, making 4,857 runs at 43.37 with 11 hundreds. He was part of the Australian sides that won the World Test Championship and the World Cup in 2023, making a fifty in the World Cup final.

What made him special

He was a batter of great patience and endless preparation. At Adelaide in 2021–22 he made a hundred from 305 balls. Before a tour of Pakistan he practised on his Brisbane balcony on a rubber mat dotted with taped metal sheeting, to copy the bounce and turn he expected there.

His leg-spin was an act of hope as much as a weapon. Fifteen Test wickets at 56.80 suggests it worked from time to time, and in 2024–25 he tried his hand at medium pace instead.

Away from the middle

Coffee is his other passion. He did a barista course at 21 and took a commercial coffee machine on tour with Australia; for the trip to Pakistan he packed 30 kg of beans for the team. His chocolate Labrador, Milo, has made appearances in backyard cricket on his Instagram.

In 2024 he was made captain of Queensland. He follows the Brisbane Broncos in rugby league and the Brisbane Lions in Australian football.

And finally

In November 2010 he had a job at the Gabba operating a Hot Spot camera for television, and was there to see Peter Siddle take an Ashes hat-trick on his birthday. A few years later the cameras were pointing at him instead.
